question: How does one plugin site become a terminal surface node — which rows are held, when is the engine answer read, and what does the boundary and the failure note do?
answer: 8 blocks are copied verbatim (4,823 units) into one module. A terminal site is drawn by `yt`: the walker produces the tree, each drawn value answers through the plugin context built from component and request id, and the draw callback receives the input the drawn descriptor names (`uo`). `pr` wraps the tree in the error boundary unless the component is a Pane; the fallback redraws the engine sentinel tree, and a caught throw notes the site as thrown, files one render-failure note and hands the tree to `onThrown`. `ur` resolves the on-screen input only while the terminal is fullscreen and the site is hooked; it reads the held rows and the asked range from the render accounting, attaches `onScreen` to the props and keeps the last rows as a fallback. `xr` reads the settled answer for the current render version, subscribes to the engine render service while hooked, bumps the mount counter, and maps a thrown promise to the engine sentinel through `onThrown`. `hdn` composes the surface node: the Box carries the drawn site ref, the render event and component, the held-row height and the overflow decision; while hooked it draws the rendered tree under the boundary, and while pending its first frame draws the fallback text. The row helpers keep the held rows stable: a changed draw or a filled content clears them, turning off stores the last rows, and the first empty content restores them. The failure note is deduplicated by component and teller (`s5t`/`Iye`), and its module list is the plugins that contributed to the settled site, or every candidate when no site is recorded (`pIn`).
measured: `cr(input, input)` is `C\u0000r\u000080\u0000false\u0000<sha256 of {}>` and `cr(null, input)` is the empty string; `dr` logs the failed site and answers undefined.
`lr` clears the rows when the content fills them or the draw changes, and clears `wasOff` on a steady draw; `mr` turns off into the last rows, and an input change still turns off.
`fr` answers undefined while on and the last rows while off.
`ur` off answers the input untouched with no site and no rows; in fullscreen it answers the drawn site, the input with `onScreen`, last rows 4 and content rows 7 from the row host.
`xr` with no hook answers undefined drawn; with a hosted answer and a matching origin it answers the settled tree; a hooked pending answer settles through the store, not the returned object.
`$e` on an empty store is `"0"`; `VH` merges the props and the terminal store viewport into the terminal input.

`yt` builds a context element whose only child is the walked tree; `pr` keeps a Pane bare and wraps every other component in `XD` with resetKey, fallback, telemetryMessage, onError and the tree child.

`hdn` draws a Box with ref, flexDirection, renderEvent, renderComponent, drawPending, minHeight and overflow; without a matching hook its child is the drawn fallback, with one it is the `XD` boundary, and `hasThrown` is the predicate closure `le` returns.

`TU` is the node of `hdn`; `ar(true)` is false and `ar(false)` is true; `uo` answers the third argument unless the drawn descriptor names the same component; `CAt` reads the descriptor input; `pIn` falls back to every candidate and answers the `kAt` descriptor.
A Pane component bypasses the boundary; `GPn(input, [component])` lists the one installed module; `Fss` returns a release function per mount.

Matcher/slice preconditions: the error-boundary component `XD`, the telemetry message stub `i5t`, the logger `t`, the control-character class `y$` and the notification sinks `aCe`/`zz` were already product-side.

partition.remaining: Partition 4 (the plugin chain runner) is complete through its terminal glue. The next ready item is C-1 (Magpie startup and recovery), with A-1 still a user action.

blocks.note: the terminal glue: `yt` renders one tree through the draw callback, `pr` adds the boundary, the row helpers keep the held rows, `ur` resolves the on-screen input, `xr` reads the settled answer, `hdn`/`TU` assemble the surface node, `VH` names the terminal input
`uo` — the input a drawn site answers when its descriptor names the same component
`bVe` — the WeakMap from a drawn site to its render descriptor, with `CAt` reading one input
`cce`/`HM`/`s5t`/`sIn`/`CK`/`Iye` — the render-failure note: dedupe slot, warning log and notification
`cIn`/`dIn` — the failure-note key and the thrown-while-drawn label
`fno`/`Lur`/`Vss` — the module list behind one settled site, filtered to the plugins that contributed
`mno`/`uIn` — the failure text and the one note per component/teller key
`pIn` — the modules a render-failure note names: the settled site contributing plugins, or every candidate

decisiveFact: The terminal surface is one node per site, not a component tree walk at this layer: `hdn` decides the rows, the render version and the drawn answer, and hands the tree to the walker only while a hook matches. The held-row state survives off-screen draws because the row helpers keep the last measured height until the content changes; the engine answer is read through a versioned cache, so a redraw without a version bump reuses the settled tree.

hostBoundary.reason: The engine that answers a render (`che`), its settled-evaluation cache (`dce`), the frame row accounting (`g4n`), the render-version mount counter (`Fss`) and the terminal mode (`Mi`) belong to the engine/host; the copied glue is the only caller. The host module mirrors the source contracts the glue reads and keeps the engine injectable. `dce.uiRender` delegates evaluation to the injected render service instead of copying the engine pipeline (`gno`) whose dependency closure is the next subsystem, not this package.
